standard_prerequisites.use: When the ring map is surjective every R-submodule is automatically an S-submodule, which yields equality.

core_obligations: Turn an arbitrary S-filtration of M into an R-filtration of M and conclude that the R-length is at least the S-length, since the R-length is the supremum over all such filtrations (proof lines 12669-12670).
In the surjective case, observe that every R-submodule is automatically an S-submodule, so the two classes of filtrations coincide and the lengths are equal (proof lines 12671-12673).
proof_roadmap: Restrict scalars along R to S on the filtrations to get the inequality (proof lines 12668-12670).
In the surjective case, note that submodules cannot be told apart, giving equality (proof lines 12671-12674).
difficulty_reason: For a ring map from R to S and an S-module M the lemma states that the R-length dominates the S-length, with equality when the ring map is surjective (statement lines 12661-12666). The proof does not estimate lengths of individual quotients: it says that a filtration by S-submodules is in particular a filtration by R-submodules, so the R-length, being a supremum over more filtrations, is at least the S-length; in the surjective case the two classes of submodules coincide, giving equality (proof lines 12668-12674). The observation that the two length functions quantify over nested classes of filtrations is the content. H2.
